skill.name: file-organizer
skill.description: Helps users organize local folders by analyzing file types, duplicates, dates, and clutter patterns, then proposing a reviewed cleanup plan.
skill.summary: Guides safe local file cleanup, duplicate review, archiving, and folder restructuring.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences, inline paths, and example prompts. Confirmed concerns are limited to shell examples that inspect local folders or move user files. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found, but broad file modification creates a real data-loss risk.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use user-selected directory placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Quote paths, avoid direct shell string interpolation, and prefer tool APIs or argument arrays where possible.

remediation.issue: File moves and deletion decisions can cause data loss.
remediation.suggestion: Require a dry run, backup reminder, explicit approval, and undo manifest before any changes.

remediation.issue: Broad directory cleanup can expose sensitive local filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend one target folder at a time and exclude sensitive paths by default.
Replace placeholders with safe reviewed examples or require a user-approved command plan.

content.value_statement: Messy folders make files hard to find and backups harder to trust. This skill reviews local folders, proposes a clear structure, and guides safe moves, renames, archiving, and duplicate cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Reviews folder contents to summarize file types, sizes, age ranges, and visible clutter patterns.
Finds likely duplicate files by names, hashes, sizes, and modification dates when requested.
Proposes folder structures for downloads, documents, projects, photos, archives, and shared work.
Guides approved folder creation, moves, renames, archiving, and duplicate cleanup.
Produces a change summary and simple maintenance habits after organization work.
limitations: It needs permission to inspect local folders before it can make useful recommendations.
It cannot guarantee duplicate choices without reviewing file contents and user preferences.
Shell commands and file metadata behavior may differ between operating systems.
It should not delete or move files without a reviewed plan and explicit approval.

use_cases.title: Clean Personal Downloads
use_cases.description: Sort mixed downloads into clear folders for documents, images, installers, archives, and files needing review.

use_cases.title: Separate Active and Archived Projects
use_cases.description: Review project folders, identify stale work, and propose a structure for active, archived, and template projects.

use_cases.title: Prepare Files for Backup
use_cases.description: Find duplicates, organize important files, and create a cleaner structure before backup or migration.

prompt_templates.title: Organize One Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me organize my Downloads folder. First analyze what is there, then propose a folder plan before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find Duplicates Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Find duplicate files in my Documents folder. Show each group, recommend which file to keep, and ask before deleting anything.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure Project Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Projects folder and separate active work, archived work, learning projects, and reusable templates. Give me a dry run first.

prompt_templates.title: Create Maintenance Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a monthly file maintenance workflow for my main work folders, including duplicate checks, archive rules, and review checkpoints.

output: Current state: documents, images, installers, and old archives are mixed together.
Suggested structure: Documents, Images, Installers, Archives, and Needs Review.
Next step: review the move plan before any file changes.
The review found several likely duplicate groups with matching names, sizes, and dates.
Each group includes a recommended file to keep and files that need approval before deletion.
Active projects, old projects, learning folders, and templates are separated in the plan.
The output lists proposed moves, uncertain folders, and a rollback log requirement.

best_practices: Start with one folder and review the proposed plan before changes begin.
Keep an undo log for every move, rename, archive, or deletion decision.
Archive uncertain files before deletion so recovery remains possible.
anti_patterns: Running cleanup across the full home directory without exclusions.
Deleting duplicate files based only on names or file sizes.
Moving active project files before confirming ownership and current work status.

faq.question: Does this skill delete files automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the agent to ask for approval before deleting files, but users should still review each plan.

faq.question: Can it organize my whole computer?
faq.answer: It can help, but a focused folder is safer and easier to verify.

faq.question: How does it find duplicates?
faq.answer: It suggests comparing hashes, names, sizes, dates, and user context.

faq.question: Can it use Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I do before large cleanup?
faq.answer: Create a backup, identify excluded folders, and request a dry run with a full move list.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive files?
faq.answer: Use narrow scopes, exclude private folders, and inspect command plans before allowing local file access.
